extracted.intended_audience: broadcasters, broadcast station managers, and broadcast attorneys advising stations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical regulatory guidance and compliance standards for U.S. radio and television broadcasters, covering FCC rules, filing deadlines, ownership limits, public file obligations, political ad rules, and enforcement risks. Includes explanations of legal standards, examples of enforcement actions, and procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marijuana advertising legality (Schedule I vs III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical marijuana moved from Schedule I to Schedule III for FDA-approved products and state-licensed medical marijuana; recreational marijuana remains Schedule I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DOJ/DEA Order affects only FDA-approved marijuana products and state medical marijuana distributed under a state medical marijuana license. Schedule III status may over time permit advertising, but marijuana remains a controlled substance whose marketing is regulated; recreational marijuana advertising remains prohibited under federal law. The DOJ/hearing process may address advertising legality later.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC early license renewal orders (call-in of renewals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC may order a broadcast station to file its license renewal applications early if review of the renewal application is 'essential' to an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used rarely; grounds include ongoing investigations where additional review is appropriate. Early filing can be used to continue inquiries and assess public interest obligations; such actions can prompt criticism and claims of selective enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent Decree compliance and conditional renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: License grants conditioned on compliance with Consent Decree terms and future adherence to FCC rules; subsequent violations can modify or shrink renewal terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a Consent Decree that promised an 8-year renewal in exchange for a voluntary contribution was modified to a one-year short-term renewal after the licensee failed to timely upload a required Q1 Issues/Programs List. Stations must meet post-decree obligations promptly or face harsher renewal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audible Crawl Rule requirements and waiver process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Audible Crawl Rule requires TV broadcasters to provide an audio description on the SAP channel of visual, nontextual emergency information displayed during non-newscast programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Media Bureau has repeatedly granted waivers due to technical unavailability; the Bureau proposed dropping the requirement if a textual on-screen crawl conveys the same information and the text is aired on the SAP channel. Waiver extensions have been routine when technical means are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS) reporting (voluntary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing DIRS reports of operating status during disasters is voluntary for broadcasters but the FCC has considered streamlining reporting and adding a 'one-click' filing option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft orders may change filing burdens; current approach under consideration does not make DIRS mandatory but seeks to reduce burdens for voluntary participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign ownership limits under Section 310(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 310(b) generally prohibits foreign entities from holding more than 20% of an FCC licensee and more than 25% of a U.S. entity directly or indirectly controlling an FCC licensee without FCC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to exceed these limits (e.g., Paramount's petition) require public comment and FCC review; approvals may request specific limitations for particular foreign investors and consider public interest implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest review for station assignments and ownership waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants seek assignment/transfer or waivers of ownership limits, the FCC evaluates public interest benefits and harms and whether a special public interest showing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent Bureau approvals have sometimes found no special showing needed when legal precedent (e.g., court vacaturs) reduces restraints; commenters can argue harms (e.g., higher retransmission consent fees). The Bureau examines impacts on local news and programming offerings in reaching a public interest conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPFM application requirements: localism and minimum distance separation
rubrics_metrics.description: LPFM applications must meet LPFM localism requirements and minimum distance separation rules; clerical errors causing violations can lead to dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau affirmed dismissals where proposals violated localism (e.g., transmitter site hundreds of miles off target) or used the wrong channel. FCC policies prohibit LPFM applicants from filing curative amendments to correct certain clerical errors that caused dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly Issues/Programs List obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-power radio and TV stations must upload Quarterly Issues/Programs Lists to their Online Public Inspection Files identifying community issues and the programs that addressed them for the quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines (e.g., April 10 for Q1) are strict; untimely uploads have led to numerous fines. These lists are the official records of how a station serves its community; prepare carefully and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lowest Unit Rate / Lowest Unit Charge obligations for political advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters must extend their lowest unit rate (LUR/LUC) to legally qualified candidates during defined windows: 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC guidance has extended LUC obligations to joint fundraising committees and 'coordinated expenditures' in some situations. Stations must compute and apply LURs correctly during political windows and monitor state-specific opening dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Public File Reports and Mid-Term EEO Review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stations with 5+ full-time employees must upload Annual EEO Public File Reports to their OPIFs; a station employment unit with thresholds (e.g., 11+ employees) triggers a Mid-Term EEO Review analyzing the last two Annual Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be uploaded and linked on station homepages where applicable. Deadlines (e.g., June 1 in some states) are consequential; late or incomplete EEO filings can lead to fines and trigger additional FCC review.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC hoax rule — Section 73.1217
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 73.1217 prohibits running information about a 'crime or catastrophe' if (1) the broadcaster knows the information is false, (2) it is reasonably foreseeable that the broadcast will cause substantial public harm, and (3) public harm is in fact caused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public harm includes direct/actual damage to property or health/safety, or diversion of law enforcement/public safety resources. Violations can result in fines and affect license renewal; exercise caution with April Fools’ or hoax programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plugola / sponsorship identification and conflict-of-interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Station employees must disclose financial interests in commercial products or services they promote on air so the public knows the promoter benefits financially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC enforcement attention to conflicts of interest (including references to plugola rules) means stations should ensure proper disclosures and sponsorship identifications to avoid enforcement or renewal issues tied to perceived undisclosed motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pirate radio enforcement and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC’s Enforcement Bureau issues Notices of Illegal Pirate Radio Broadcasting and may impose large fines under applicable statutes (example fine amount cited up to $2,453,218).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landowners and licensees permitting pirate operations can receive enforcement notices; continuing violations risk substantial fines and further enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: FM translator interference complaint standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC’s translator interference rules require a minimum of six listener complaints from separate locations to demonstrate that a translator is causing actual interference to a full-power station.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints need not be geographically dispersed in every case (small zones of interference may result in clustered complaints). The Bureau cautioned against using the complaint process for private financial gain and notes that monetary settlements from voluntary dismissals should be limited to reimbursement of expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: FARA notification requirement for U.S.-based foreign media outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S.-based foreign media outlets classified as 'an agent of a foreign government' under the Foreign Agents Registration Act must notify the FCC of their relationship to and funding from a foreign government or political party by specified deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to companies providing video programming to cable and satellite systems; the FCC reports to Congress on these operations every six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports media marketplace factors for FCC inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC’s inquiry seeks comment on competition in the video and audio marketplaces, including streaming platforms’ impact on broadcasters, sports rights contracts, public access to live sports, and the FCC’s authority to ensure access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasters should comment if affected; issues include fragmentation of sports rights, importance of free broadcast sports for underserved viewers, and proposals to relax ownership rules to help broadcasters compete for rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver standards for national TV ownership cap and local ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking to exceed the national TV ownership cap or local duopoly rules may seek waivers; the FCC evaluates whether granting a waiver serves the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent Bureau decisions have granted waivers when benefits (e.g., expanded local news/programming, inability of out-of-market competitors to operate a standalone service) outweigh harms. Courts and commenters may challenge such waivers; decisions reference precedent and market-specific analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign sponsorship identification rules for broadcasters
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial full-power TV, Class A TV, and AM/FM radio stations must comply with foreign sponsorship identification requirements beginning on specified compliance dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stations should implement required sponsor ID practices (e.g., disclosures when programming or paid material is provided by a foreign entity) by the compliance date (example cited: June 7) to avoid violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory fee payment obligations and Order to Pay or Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees with delinquent regulatory fees can receive an Order to Pay or to Show Cause proposing revocation unless debts (fees, interest, administrative costs, penalties) are paid or justified within a set timeframe (e.g., 60 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely resolve outstanding regulatory fee debts can lead to license revocation proceedings; stations must monitor and timely pay fiscal-year regulatory fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Public Inspection File (OPIF) upload and website link requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stations must timely upload required documents (Quarterly Issues/Programs Lists, EEO reports, certain fundraising and foreign programming disclosures) to their OPIFs and include a link to the uploaded annual EEO report on the station home page if the station has a website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and completeness are strictly enforced; missing or late uploads have resulted in fines and renewal complications. Examples include Q1 Issues/Programs Lists and annual EEO reports.
